note: Append-only activity log. The verification pipeline writes an entry for every field-level change it makes; humans write entries for decisions. This is what the /updates page renders, and it is the audit trail that makes an autonomous board trustworthy.

kinds.changed: A tracked field changed on an existing entry
kinds.verified: Confidence moved up — a claim got corroborated or confirmed
kinds.missed: A deadline passed without us acting

updates.title: Fixed a fabricated-outcome bug — 5 events wrongly shown as "entered"
updates.body: scripts/sync_radar.py's to_radar_past() defaulted any dropped_or_past entry with no missed flag and no result to outcome "entered". Five entries were just discovery notes ("ran on X date, diarise for next year") we never actually applied to — ITWeb Security Summit Hackathon, MICT SETA National Skills Challenge, Monkey and River Hackathon, GirlCode Pan-African Hackathon, Geekulcha SS26Hack Kimberley — and the site was showing all five as things the team entered. Fixed to skip syncing any dropped_or_past entry with no real engagement signal instead of guessing. Only genuine participation (Discovery Gradhack, Top 6) remains on the Season So Far list.

updates.title: Africa Deep Tech Challenge 2026 — decided not to compete
updates.body: Team decision: not entering the Laptop LLM Challenge. Status moved to dropped; archived off the live board.

updates.title: UNESCO Youth Hackathon 2026 — submitted
updates.body: Submitted HAYIBO: an interactive toolkit teaching South Africans — especially digitally illiterate and older audiences — to spot AI deepfakes and misinformation the way it actually spreads locally (WhatsApp voice notes, Facebook, radio call-in), via five spoken verification questions that need no reading or device. Taught through a weekly two-clip real-vs-AI guessing game run simultaneously on WhatsApp, Facebook (public leaderboard) and community radio (elders phone in and reason aloud). Every round is logged by language and platform and published openly — the first public dataset of AI-generated misinformation in isiZulu, Sepedi and other SA languages. Deliverables sent: proposal document, 9-slide pitch deck, 2:57 narrated video pitch. Confirmation email received; results expected mid-September 2026. Status moved to submitted.

updates.body: Fetched every link in data/opportunities.json with a real User-Agent and followed redirects. 40 of 44 resolved cleanly. Corrections: (1) IBM Z Datathon linked an ENDED prior Devpost edition (Sept 24-25, 'This hackathon has ended') — removed, and the prize pool taken from that same stale page corrected from $30,000 to the organiser's stated $50,000+; dates 17-18 Oct 2026 independently confirmed correct. (2) Geekulcha hackathon.gklink.co no longer resolves in DNS — replaced with gklink.co. (3) FNB appoftheyear.co.za returns 500 on / and 404 on /hackathon — primary link moved to the live 22 On Sloane partner page, official URL retained. (4) Entelect www.entelect.co.za redirected to the apex domain — pointed straight at it. Huawei's e.huawei.com 403s to automated checks but is a bot block, not a dead page, and was deliberately left alone.

updates.title: Mintek SCI Grad Hackathon 2026 — team SELECTED
updates.body: Official selection letter received, dated 14 Aug 2026, signed Boitumelo Lekalakala. Status moved from applied to selected, confidence to confirmed, lifecycle to committed. Confirmed: cash prizes R25k/R15k/R10k (1st/2nd/3rd), possible vacation-work offers for standout teams. Immediate action: one-page abstract due 30 Aug 2026, plus per-member ID number/T-shirt size/contact details/mentor info back to Mintek. Final hacking day is mandatory in-person at Mintek on 1 Oct 2026 (build from 08:00, code submission deadline 13:00, presentations from 14:00, 10 min/team). Must also register for and attend the Mintek SCI Conference on 2 Oct 2026, where the 5 finalist teams are announced and originality/AI-generation/plagiarism authentication begins for the next stage.

updates.title: Mintek-SCi Grad Hackathon 2026 — REEFPRINT abstract recorded
updates.body: Added the submitted abstract to what_to_build: REEFPRINT (Problem 3 — Computer Vision for Real-Time Mineralogical Characterisation), by Lethabo. Distills SEM/XRD/QEMSCAN output into a fast optical model across five Bushveld phases, reports per-class recall on sub-1% base-metal sulphide ahead of aggregate accuracy, converts texture into liberation/reagent demand/grindability with calibrated abstention, costs in Rand/tCO2e, and is positioned as a StarCS/FloatStar/MillStar module.

updates.title: Board widened from hackathons to opportunities
updates.body: Added a `kind` field so the board covers competitions, graduate programmes, recruiting events and accelerators — not just hackathons. Two entries were reclassified on migration: BCG Platinion is a `recruiting_event` (the event is the interview) and Mintek-SCi is a `grad_programme`. Also added `career_track` to mark the three entries that are direct hiring routes.

updates.title: Discovery Gradhack 2026 — missed by three days
updates.body: Ran 7 August 2026 at Discovery Place, Sandton. 50 IT students from SA universities, teams of 2–4, free entry, R12 500 per winning team member, plus a permanent-employment pathway. It was the board's #1 open action item and the only signal was an empty team calendar. Moved to past. Predicted-window watch set for ~August 2027.

updates.title: ADTC prize conflict closed — arithmetic confirms the earlier ruling
updates.body: Press reported "$20,000+" against Devpost's itemised $16,500. Confirmed by arithmetic that both are correct and describe different things: 8000+4000+3000+1500 = $16,500 cash, and 10×$250 + 20×$50 = $3,500 in GPU credits, totalling exactly $20,000. No action needed.

updates.title: ADTC — possible second stage, unresolved
updates.body: Sources still report 25 August against the board's 24 August, and one describes it as a "first-stage deadline" for "initial proposals". The board models this as a single submit-once deadline. Keeping Devpost's earlier date — submitting early is free — but flagged for a manual check of the organiser page before the 24th.

updates.title: Initial board — 17 entries, calendar, playbook, CLI
updates.body: First full research pass. Every date carries a source link and a confidence level; conflicts recorded with the reasoning behind each ruling.
